fetchHead.observation: FETCH_HEAD's mtime has advanced multiple times across this unit's own investigation window, during which this unit performed zero network operations. This is consistent with an external, independent process (most plausibly the IDE's own periodic background auto-fetch, given the multiple active editor processes observed in the prior unit's process listing) continuing to touch this file on its own schedule. This is NOT attributable to this checkpoint-85 unit and is NOT a repeat of the originally-disclosed dry-run. It is reported here for completeness because Phase 2 required inspecting FETCH_HEAD's current state, not because this unit caused it.

currentLocalEvidenceInspected.remoteTrackingRefReflogInterpretation: The most recent entry that ever changed refs/remotes/origin/feature/source-availability-engine-v1 is 'update by push', not a fetch. No fetch-attributed entry exists anywhere in this ref's reflog. This is deterministic local evidence that neither the disclosed dry-run nor any subsequent fetch-like event has moved this ref since the authorized push.
currentLocalEvidenceInspected.headReflog: @{0} is the evidence-tail commit itself (a commit, not a fetch/checkout entry). git fetch, dry-run or otherwise, never writes HEAD, the index, or the working tree under any circumstances -- this is a structural property of Git, not something that requires per-instance verification.

objectDatabaseCheck.method: git fsck --unreachable --dangling (local only), plus targeted (non-recursive) mtime inspection of a sample of unreachable blobs and of the pack directory
objectDatabaseCheck.sampleResult: All 5 sampled unreachable blobs live inside pack files, not as loose objects. The containing packs have mtimes of 2026-06-06 and 2026-07-20 -- weeks before this operation and long before the disclosed fetch. None is attributable to the disclosed fetch.
packDirectoryFindings: pack-be0d07d00a9b598b84635367b6644c8d32b3594b.pack mtime 2026-08-08T07:31:42+08:00 -- coincides exactly with the substantive C37 commit's timestamp, consistent with automatic Git housekeeping around that commit, not the fetch.

pack-684b7b9c6a1276fbd77ece59c8eb252296a6224e.pack mtime 2026-08-08T09:42:24+08:00 -- precedes the disclosed fetch (09:44:20) by roughly two minutes, consistent with automatic Git housekeeping around the evidence-tail commit (09:39:11) or push (09:43:35-09:43:43), not the fetch.

No pack or loose object was found with a creation/modification time inside or after the disclosed fetch's window that is not otherwise explained by the commit/push that this unit already has full evidence for.
objectDatabaseCheck.conclusion: No object in the local database can be specifically attributed to the disclosed dry-run fetch. A dry-run fetch does not transfer objects by design, and this local evidence is consistent with that design: the large unreachable-object count is pre-existing repository history debris (e.g. from an earlier hard reset visible in the reflog: 'reset: moving to ee664eab...'), unrelated to this deviation.

classificationRationale: This is not classified as A (no impact) merely because --dry-run was used: FETCH_HEAD demonstrably was written, both by the originally disclosed fetch and, independently, by at least one later, unrelated background process this unit did not initiate. That is real, observable local Git metadata impact. It is not classified as C (unresolved) because every one of the seven determination questions above was answered from direct, checkable local evidence, not supposition. It is not classified as D (substantive repository impact) because zero refs, zero objects, zero index state, and zero working-tree content are attributable to it.
